newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude firmer, helped by U.S. gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude firmer, helped by U.S. gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude was firmer and nudging session highs on Monday afternoon helped by stronger U.S. gasoline in a modest partial correction of last week's slide, brokers said.
Dec Brent crude was up 17 cents at $22.67 a barrel by 1534 GMT, three cents off the session high posted early on Monday.
"U.S. gasoline is helping but this market was also in need of a correction. Brent was looking oversold," said a broker.
NYMEX gasoline put on over a cent a gallon, supported by concern supply will tighten as U.S. refiners maximise distillate output.
"One missile isn't going to change things over there," said one broker.
Brokers said the market would now wait to see the next weekly data on U.S. oil stock levels, due to be released after the close on Tuesday.
"Another big build in U.S. heating oil stocks and we could test $200 (on prompt IPE gas oil)," said one.
But this broker and others said the market would not collapse this early into winter and a time when heating oil stocks still remain well below 1995 levels.
IPE gas oil was weaker, however, covering ground lost by Brent in a late selloff on Friday after the contract had closed.
Nov gas oil lost $1.00 to $211.00 a tonne by 1547 GMT. Dec was steadier, slipping just 25 cents, trimming the prompt backwardation to $4.25.
Dealers said Brent was expected to recover after five consecutive lower closes posted in London last week, when crude futures shed over $1.50 a barrel.
News on Monday of a second U.S. missile strike against an Iraqi anti-aircraft site in three days provided mild support to prices but the impact was short-lived, brokers said.
